claim: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ that makes it easy to set up and operate message brokers in the cloud.
question: What is Amazon MQ?

values.display: managed message broker service
Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ

evidence.quote: Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ that makes it easy to set up and operate message brokers in the cloud.

claim: Amazon MQ gives you industry-standard messaging APIs and protocols, including JMS, NMS, AMQP 0.9.1, AMQP 1.0, STOMP, MQTTv3 and WebSocket, and direct access to the ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ consoles.
question: Which industry-standard messaging APIs and protocols can you use with Amazon MQ?

values.display: JMS, NMS, AMQP 0.9.1, AMQP 1.0, STOMP, MQTTv3, and WebSocket
industry standard APIs and protocols for messaging

evidence.quote: You can directly access the ActiveMQ console, RabbitMQ console, industry standard APIs and protocols for messaging, including JMS, NMS, AMQP 0.9.1, AMQP 1.0, STOMP, MQTTv3, and WebSocket.

claim: Amazon MQ is compatible with common messaging APIs such as JMS and NMS and protocols including AMQP, STOMP, MQTT and WebSocket, so you can switch from any standards-based message broker without rewriting the messaging code in your applications.
question: How do I migrate if I am using a different message broker instead of ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ?

values.display: switch from any standards-based message broker
without rewriting the messaging code

evidence.quote: Amazon MQ provides compatibility with the most common messaging APIs, such as Java Message Service (JMS) and .NET Message Service (NMS), and protocols, including AMQP, STOMP, MQTT, and WebSocket. This makes it easy to switch from any standards-based message broker to Amazon MQ without rewriting the messaging code in your applications.

claim: In most cases you only need to update the endpoints of your Amazon MQ broker for your existing applications to connect and start sending messages.
question: What do I usually have to change in an existing application to use Amazon MQ?

values.display: simply update the endpoints
start sending messages

qualifiers.scope: existing applications moving to Amazon MQ

evidence.quote: In most cases, you can simply update the endpoints of your Amazon MQ broker to connect to your existing applications, and start sending messages.

claim: Amazon MQ suits teams that plan to adopt industry-standard messaging APIs and protocols to decouple and scale their applications on the cloud without the operational burden of managing the message broker.
question: Who should use Amazon MQ?

values.display: industry standard messaging APIs and protocols
without the operational burden of managing the message broker

evidence.quote: Amazon MQ is suitable for enterprise IT professionals, developers, and architects who plan to adopt industry standard messaging APIs and protocols to decouple and scale their applications on the cloud without the operational burden of managing the message broker itself.

claim: Amazon MQ sets up the message broker and provisions the infrastructure and open-source engine software. After the broker runs, Amazon manages ongoing software upgrades, security updates, fault detection and recovery.
question: What does Amazon MQ manage on my behalf?

values.display: provisioning the infrastructure and open-source broker engine software
software upgrades, security updates, fault detection, and recovery

evidence.quote: Amazon MQ manages the process of setting up a message broker and provisioning the infrastructure and open-source broker engine software. Once your broker is up and running, Amazon manages ongoing software upgrades, security updates, fault detection, and recovery.

claim: In a multi-AZ deployment, Amazon MQ automatically manages the nodes, replicates data for high availability, deploys patches regularly, manages integrations with AWS services, makes important metrics visible and supports broker engine version upgrades.
question: What does Amazon MQ do automatically in a multi-AZ deployment broker?

values.display: replicates data for high availability
deploys patches regularly

evidence.quote: Amazon MQ automatically manages the nodes in the deployment, replicates data for high availability, deploys patches regularly, manages integrations with AWS services, makes important metrics visible, and supports broker engine version upgrades so you can take advantage of the latest improvements to the open-source versions.

claim: With Amazon MQ you do not handle broker provisioning, security patching, setup, configuration, version upgrades or recovery. Consider it when you want to offload operational overhead and the costs that go with it.
question: When would I use Amazon MQ versus managing ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ on Amazon EC2 myself?

values.display: offload operational overhead
broker provisioning, security patching, setup, configuration, broker version upgrades, or recovery

qualifiers.scope: Amazon MQ versus self-managed on EC2

evidence.quote: With Amazon MQ, you do not have to worry about administration tasks such as broker provisioning, security patching, setup, configuration, broker version upgrades, or recovery. You may want to consider Amazon MQ when you want to offload operational overhead and associated costs.

claim: If you want greater control to customize features and configurations, or to use custom plugins, consider installing and running your message broker on Amazon EC2 directly instead of using Amazon MQ.
question: When should I run ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ on Amazon EC2 myself instead of using Amazon MQ?

values.display: greater control to customize features and configurations
custom plugins

qualifiers.scope: Amazon MQ versus self-managed on EC2

evidence.quote: If you want greater control to customize features and configurations or to use custom plugins, you may want to consider installing and running your message broker on Amazon EC2 directly.

claim: Amazon MQ does not charge for inter-node data transfer for RabbitMQ brokers. On a self-managed RabbitMQ cluster that transfer can be a high cost.
question: Do I pay for inter-node data transfer on Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ?

values.display: does not charge for inter-node data transfer
high costs on a self-managed cluster

evidence.quote: In certain use cases, the inter-node data transfer for RabbitMQ can result in high costs on a self-managed cluster. Amazon MQ does not charge for inter-node data transfer for RabbitMQ brokers.

claim: Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ supports two broker storage types: durability optimized, using Amazon EFS, and throughput optimized, using Amazon EBS.
question: What type of storage is available with Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ?

values.display: durability optimized using Amazon Elastic File System
throughput optimized using Amazon Elastic Block Store

evidence.quote: Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ supports two types of broker storage – durability optimized using Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) and throughput optimized using Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS).

claim: For high durability and replication across multiple Availability Zones, use durability optimized ActiveMQ brokers backed by Amazon EFS. For high throughput in high-volume applications, use throughput optimized brokers backed by EBS.
question: When do I choose EFS-backed or EBS-backed storage for an Amazon MQ for ActiveMQ broker?

values.display: high durability and replication across multiple Availability Zones
high throughput for your high-volume applications

evidence.quote: To take advantage of high durability and replication across multiple Availability Zones, use durability optimized brokers backed by Amazon EFS. To take advantage of high throughput for your high-volume applications, use throughput optimized brokers backed by EBS.

claim: A network of brokers is multiple ActiveMQ brokers connected in a mesh. The brokers share information about the clients and destinations each one hosts and use it to route messages through the network.
question: What is an Amazon MQ network of brokers?

values.display: multiple brokers connected in a mesh
route messages through the network

evidence.quote: A network of brokers consists of multiple brokers connected in a mesh. Brokers in the network share information about the clients and destinations each broker hosts. The brokers use this information to route messages through the network.

claim: In an Amazon MQ network of brokers, each broker is either an active-standby broker, whose standby node with shared storage takes over if the active node fails, or a single-instance broker, which is unavailable after a node failure until it is restarted.
question: What broker types can a network of brokers contain on Amazon MQ, and what happens on failure?

values.display: active-standby brokers
unavailable until it is restarted

evidence.quote: With Amazon MQ, the brokers in the network can either be active-standby brokers (each active broker in the network has a standby node, with shared storage, that will take over if the active node fails), or single-instance brokers (if the node fails, it will be unavailable until it is restarted).

claim: Each broker in a network keeps its own message store, replicated across multiple Availability Zones for active/standby brokers using durability-optimized storage. Nodes forward messages to each other, so a single broker stores a given message at any time.
question: Where are messages stored in an Amazon MQ network of brokers?

values.display: its own unique message store
stored by a single broker at any given time

qualifiers.condition: replication across AZs applies to active/standby brokers with durability-optimized storage

evidence.quote: Each broker in the network maintains its own unique message store which is replicated across multiple availability zones (AZs) within a region for active/standby brokers, using durability-optimized storage. The nodes in the network forward messages to each other, so messages are stored by a single broker at any given time.

claim: Use a network of brokers if you need high availability with fast reconnection after a broker failure, or if you need to scale horizontally.
question: When should I use an Amazon MQ network of brokers?

values.display: high availability with fast reconnection
scale horizontally

evidence.quote: You should use network of brokers if you require high availability with fast reconnection in the case of broker failure, or if you need the ability to scale horizontally.

claim: For high availability you can choose a three-node cluster deployment for RabbitMQ, or an Active-Standby deployment or a mesh network of brokers for ActiveMQ.
question: How can I ensure high availability on Amazon MQ?

values.display: three-node cluster deployment for RabbitMQ
mesh network of brokers for ActiveMQ

evidence.quote: You can choose from a three-node cluster deployment for RabbitMQ, an Active-Standby deployment or a mesh network of brokers for ActiveMQ.

claim: The EC2 instances behind an Amazon MQ broker are managed by the service and are not visible in your EC2 account. Some networking resources, such as ENIs and VPC endpoints, are visible so that you can connect to the broker.
question: When I create an Amazon MQ cluster, do the underlying resources such as EC2 instances show up in my EC2 console?

values.display: EC2 instances are not visible
visible in your Amazon EC2 account

evidence.quote: No, EC2 instances are not visible in your EC2 account as these are managed by the Amazon MQ service. Some networking resources (elastic network interfaces (ENIs), VPC endpoints) are visible in your Amazon EC2 account for you to connect to the broker.

claim: With every Amazon MQ broker you provision broker instances and broker storage. You can pick an existing VPC, subnet, security group or customer managed keys instead of the ones the service provides.
question: What do I need to provision within an Amazon MQ broker?

values.display: broker instances and broker storage
customer managed keys

evidence.quote: You need to provision broker instances and broker storage with every broker you create. You may choose to select an existing VPC, subnet, security group or customer managed keys instead of the ones provided by the Amazon MQ service.

claim: Amazon MQ lets you create custom configurations and apply them to new and existing clusters.
question: Can I change the default broker configurations or upload a new configuration to Amazon MQ?

values.display: create custom configurations
new and existing clusters

evidence.quote: Yes, Amazon MQ allows you to create custom configurations and apply them to new and existing clusters.

claim: Any application that runs on an AWS compute service, such as Amazon EC2, Amazon ECS or AWS Lambda, can use Amazon MQ.
question: How does Amazon MQ work with other AWS services?

values.display: AWS compute service
Amazon EC2, Amazon ECS, or AWS Lambda

evidence.quote: Any application that runs on an AWS compute service, such as Amazon EC2, Amazon ECS, or AWS Lambda, can use Amazon MQ.

claim: Amazon MQ message brokers can be a source for AWS Lambda and for Amazon EventBridge Pipes.
question: Can Amazon MQ brokers be an event source for Lambda or EventBridge Pipes?

values.display: Use Amazon MQ message brokers as a source
AWS Lambda

evidence.quote: AWS Lambda - Use Amazon MQ message brokers as a source
AWS EventBridge Pipes – Use Amazon MQ message brokers as a source

claim: Amazon MQ integrates with Amazon CloudWatch for metrics and alarms, CloudWatch Logs for broker logs, and AWS CloudTrail for logging and retaining API calls.
question: Which AWS services does Amazon MQ integrate with for monitoring and auditing?

values.display: Monitor metrics and generate alarms
Log, continuously monitor, and retain Amazon MQ API calls

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudWatch - Monitor metrics and generate alarms
Amazon CloudWatch Logs - Publish logs from your Amazon MQ brokers to Amazon CloudWatch Logs
AWS CloudTrail - Log, continuously monitor, and retain Amazon MQ API calls

claim: Amazon MQ integrates with AWS CloudFormation to automate creating, updating and deleting brokers, with IAM for authentication and authorization of the service API, and with AWS KMS for the keys that encrypt your data.
question: Which AWS services does Amazon MQ integrate with for automation, access control and encryption?

values.display: Automate the process of creating, updating, and deleting message brokers
Create and control keys used to encrypt your data

evidence.quote: AWS CloudFormation - Automate the process of creating, updating, and deleting message brokers
AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) - Authentication and authorization of the service API
AWS Key Management Service (KMS) - Create and control keys used to encrypt your data
